items.summary: Fiona the hippo, the beloved star of the Cincinnati Zoo for nearly a decade, has died after she ate a visitor’s hat that was accidentally tossed into her enclosure, despite tireless efforts to save her. Now, tributes are pouring in and some are demanding answers. NBC’s Maggie Vespa reports for TODAY.

items.originalTitle: Tokyo's hidden methane: Survey pinpoints nearly 100 hot spots
items.title: Tokyo's hidden methane: Survey pinpoints nearly 100 hot spots
items.summary: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) has been the poster child of climate change, but another culprit could be flying just under the radar. Methane is a potent greenhouse gas with a global warming potential approximately 84 times greater than that of CO₂ over a 20-year period. Fortunately, methane remains in the atmosphere for only about a decade, and reducing its emissions could provide rapid climate mitigation effects.

items.originalTitle: Male bumblebees contribute to nest care, challenging view that they only mate
items.author: Jules Bernstein
items.title: Male bumblebees contribute to nest care, challenging view that they only mate
items.summary: For decades, researchers have assumed male bumblebees' contribution to hives consisted mainly of DNA. However, a new study finds that the males actually help incubate baby bumbles, and that with males' assistance, hives thrive. The study, published in the Royal Society Open Science journal, quantifies the beneficial effects of having male babysitters in the hive.

items.originalTitle: Misinformation perception shapes support of democracy in Australia
items.title: Misinformation perception shapes support of democracy in Australia
items.summary: A new study by Adelaide University researchers has found that the more often people perceived they had encountered misinformation, the less positive their views of Australian democracy tended to be. The experience-sampling study from the School of Psychology asked 123 eligible voters to track their perceived exposure to misinformation in the lead-up to the 2025 Australian federal election and measured whether this exposure influenced their attitudes and emotions toward the election.

items.originalTitle: A star's last gasps: ALMA reveals a giant gas ring and budding hourglass around a star in transition
items.title: A star's last gasps: ALMA reveals a giant gas ring and budding hourglass around a star in transition
items.summary: Stars like our sun don't die quietly. In their final act, they swell into red giants, shed their outer layers into space and leave behind a glowing, often strikingly sculpted cloud of gas called a planetary nebula. That transformation is thought to take only a few thousand years, a blink in the life of a star, so catching one in the act is rare.
